analysis: Examined three changed files against the provider threat model. (1) EngineV2KVQuantizationPolicy.swift lines 80-89: for modelType flint, the provider-wide `global` default is no longer consulted. Explicit env or per-model overrides that are non-native still throw flintRequiresNative, and the result stays .native. This is a fail-closed refinement: the checkpoint default of balanced no longer causes a spurious refusal. Flint never gets quantized checkpoint or KV precision implicitly, and I see no new exposure. It touches the prefix-cache/checkpoint at-rest surface only by keeping Flint native, which is not a widening of T-041. (2) EngineV2Factory+BackendPreparation.swift lines ~180-183 and ~222-227: for FlintModel, .auto is promoted to .paged, and any non-paged resolution, including the crash-loop guard fallback, throws pagedUnavailable. This is a stricter, fail-closed control. The residual availability effect is that a crash-loop guard now refuses a Flint load rather than degrading. That is deliberate and affects only Flint. I could not see the full function, so I did not verify that every other fallback path between the new override and the refusal check is covered. The visible patch gives no evidence of a bypass. (3) ThroughputSweep.swift lines 123-132 and 207-209: this is a benchmark-only tool. It skips the scalar prefill for flint, and it reads config.json to get the model type. Config.json is read from the operator-chosen model directory, which is not an untrusted-network boundary, so I see no attack surface. The decode path is unchanged and uses the production build with the checkpointQuantization resolved at line 77. No coordinator wire, attestation, App Attest, key custody or encryption behavior changed. Remaining integration questions: whether Flint's paged-only requirement is enforced consistently in the other construction paths (EngineV2SlotFactory, the production factory) and whether the Flint unit tests cover these behaviors. Neither is observable from the supplied units.
